steps.body: Here is the most freeing fact in this book: **intelligibility and accent are separate things.** Research (Derwing & Munro) shows a strong Pakistani accent can be 100% intelligible — and clients don't hire accents, they hire people they understand without effort. So we are NOT eliminating your accent. We are fixing the 9 specific sound problems that make Urdu/Hindi speakers hard to understand in English, in order of impact. Everything else about your accent stays — it's part of you.

**1. Word stress & rhythm (biggest impact).** English is stress-timed: some syllables are loud and long, others nearly vanish. Urdu/Hindi stress patterns applied to English (*"pho-to-GRAPH"* instead of *"PHO-to-graph"*) confuse listeners more than any single wrong sound. **Rule:** every new word you learn gets its stress marked: **PHO**-to-graph, de-**VEL**-op-ment, **CLI**-ent. Clap the stressed syllable. English rhythm = stressed syllables land like drum beats, roughly evenly spaced.

**2. /θ/ and /ð/ (thin, this).** These sounds don't exist in Urdu — speakers substitute *t/d* ("tin" for "thin", "dis" for "this"). **Fix:** put your tongue tip *between your teeth* and blow. Feel the air on your hand — that's the fricative. If your tongue isn't visible, you're saying /t/. 50 reps/day for two weeks on: thin/tin, thigh/tie, though/dough, three/tree.

steps.heading: 3. /v/ vs /w/ (very/wary).** Many Urdu/Hindi speakers merge these. **Fix
steps.body:
/v/ = top teeth touch bottom lip (*vvvv* — feel the buzz). /w/ = lips round, no teeth (*www* — like blowing out a candle). Mirror work: vest/west, vine/wine, very/wary.

**4. Consonant clusters (school, not "iskool").** Urdu resists initial clusters, so speakers insert a vowel. **Fix — backward buildup:** say "kool" → "skool" → "school". Stretch the cluster, never accept the inserted vowel in drills. Practice: school, station, please, project, street.

**5. Diphthongs (day, go).** /eɪ/ and /oʊ/ get flattened to single vowels ("de", "go"). **Fix — glide-hold:** stretch it: "daaaay", "goooow". Feel the two-vowel slide. If your mouth doesn't move, it's not a diphthong.

**6. /p/ vs /f/.** Aspiration patterns differ across the languages. **Fix — tissue test:** hold tissue before your mouth. "Pat" blows it; "fat" doesn't. Minimal pairs: pat/fat, pull/full.

**7. /ʒ/ (vision, decision).** Rare sound, low priority — but it appears in client words (*decision, revision, usual*). **Fix:** learn it inside those 10–15 words only. No drill needed beyond shadowing them.

**8. Intonation.** Urdu/Hindi melody on English statements can sound uncertain or abrupt on calls. **Fix:** English statements fall ⤵ at the end; yes/no questions rise ⤴. Shadow 5 core call sentences (below) copying the *melody*, not just words.
**9. /r/ quality.** Retroflex Urdu /r/ vs English approximant. Rarely blocks understanding — polish it last, if ever.

steps.title: Minimal-pair chant
steps.text:
Say each pair 10×, exaggerating the difference. Record the last round. Do one row per day:
- Row A (/θ/): thin–tin, thigh–tie, three–tree, thank–tank
- Row B (/ð/): this–dis, though–dough, they–day
- Row C (/v-w/): very–wary, vest–west, vine–wine
- Row D (clusters): say "kool→skool→school", "tation→station→station", "please" (no "palease")
- Row E (diphthongs): day ("daaaay"), go ("goooow"), late, phone — hold the glide 2 seconds
Self-check: play your recording. If a pair sounds identical, that pair goes on tomorrow's list too.

steps.body: Shadowing is the single best-evidenced speaking-fluency technique in the research: studies show large gains in fluency and pronunciation (including +20% pronunciation accuracy at 20 min/day over 6 weeks), plus 30–40% listening gains. Here's the exact protocol:

1. **Material:** one clear native recording, slightly above your level (BBC 6 Minute English, a TED talk, an audiobook chapter). Same clip all week (narrow input).
2. **Blind shadowing (days 1–2):** no script. Repeat 0.5–1 second behind the speaker, copying rhythm, stress, melody. Mumble along if you miss words — staying in rhythm matters more than catching every word. Start at 0.75× speed if needed.
3. **Script-checked shadowing (days 3–4):** read the transcript first, mark the stresses, then shadow. Now you know what you're saying.
4. **Selective shadowing (days 5–7):** shadow only the stressed/key words; let the small words blur past. This trains English rhythm directly.
5. **Rules:** do it privately (anxiety kills the benefit — phone recorder, your room, no audience). Never shadow as a graded performance.

**The 5 core call sentences** (intonation shadowing — copy the melody exactly):

1. *"Hi Ahmed, thanks for reaching out."* ⤵
2. *"I'll send you the quote within twenty-four hours."* ⤵
3. *"Quick heads-up: the dashboard will be ready Wednesday."* ⤵
4. *"Could you share the data file when you get a chance?"* ⤵ (polite request — slight rise, then fall)
5. *"Does that timeline work for you?"* ⤴ (yes/no question rises)

steps.title: Shadow the news
steps.text: Pick one 3-minute BBC 6 Minute English episode. Days 1–2: blind shadow. Days 3–4: script-checked. Days 5–7: selective shadowing of stressed words. Same episode all week. Log one sentence per day: "today shadowing felt ___ because ___."

steps.body:
Your ear lies to you in real time — it hears what you *meant* to say. The recorder doesn't. Method:

1. Record 60–90 seconds (a drill answer, a pitch, a call simulation).
2. Listen once WITHOUT the transcript. Mark every moment you stumble.
3. Transcribe what you actually said (painful, essential).
4. Compare against what you meant. Log the errors (Module 1 format).
5. Re-record once, fixing only the worst problem.

One cycle per day is worth more than an hour of unrecorded talking.

steps.title: Record, transcribe, flinch, fix
steps.prompt: Record yourself answering: "What did you work on this week?" (60 seconds). Transcribe it fully. Circle: dropped articles, /θ/→/t/ slips, flat intonation, filler words. Log the top 3 in your error log. Re-record once.
steps.tip: Fluency mode: no stopping, no mid-sentence correcting.

steps.prompt:
**Stress-mark the script**

Take the 5 core call sentences from Lesson 3.2. Mark the stressed syllable in CAPS in every content word ("I'll SEND you the QUOTE withIN TWENty-four HOURS"). Read them aloud 5× each, hitting the caps like drum beats. Then shadow them from a native speaker on YouGlish (type each phrase, play 5 clips at 0.5×, copy the melody).

steps.title: Quiz — Pronunciation

questions.prompt: Tongue between the teeth — which word?
Teeth on the lower lip — which word starts with /v/?
questions.explanation: bite the lower lip (west = rounded lips = /w/)

questions.prompt: No extra vowel at the start — which is correct?
questions.explanation: build it backwards: ool → skool → school

questions.prompt: Which is polite on a call?
options: "Could you please send me the files?"
questions.explanation: commands sound rude; "Could you please…" is the professional default

questions.prompt: Stretch the vowel with a glide — which is correct?
questions.explanation: hold it: daaaay, feel the glide
(speech) / going to (writing) — never "gona" to a client

questions.prompt: A statement with FALLING pitch at the end sounds…
questions.explanation: falling pitch = certain; rising pitch on statements sounds unsure

steps.rule: 8/10 to move on. Answer first, then learn from the misses.

steps.heading: Can-do statements
steps.body:
- [ ] A listener can distinguish my thin/tin, very/wary, west/vest pairs
- [ ] I never insert vowels into clusters in drills (school, station, project)
- [ ] I mark stress on every new vocabulary word
- [ ] My 5 core call sentences have falling intonation on statements, rising on yes/no questions
- [ ] I can shadow a 3-minute clip staying within 1 second of the speaker

steps.heading: Mini-test
steps.body: Record the 5 core call sentences + Row A minimal pairs. Send the audio to your AI tutor (or a Tandem partner from B1 onward) with one question: "Which words were unclear?" Their answer is your next drill list.

steps.heading: Re-entry note
steps.body:
Pronunciation decays without maintenance (research: gains fade in ~3 weeks without practice). Back after a break? One week of Drill 3.1 rows + 10 min daily shadowing before anything else.

🗣️ **Badge earned: Clear Speaker** — you are now intelligible on purpose, not by luck.
